title: A Multimodal Foundation Agent for Financial Trading: Tool-Augmented, Diversified, and Generalist

task.value: Single-asset daily trading (buy, sell or hold a stock or cryptocurrency) using a multimodal, tool-augmented LLM agent to maximize profit.
task.quote: Specifically, we focus on single asset (e.g., stock or Crypto) trading.

architecture.value: Five modules: market intelligence (news, prices, reports, with diversified retrieval), vector-store memory, low-level reflection on price movements with Kline charts, high-level reflection on past decisions with trading charts, and a tool-augmented decision module using expert guidance and rule-based strategies.
architecture.quote: FinAgent is a multimodal LLMs agent in this framework specifically designed for financial trading, which contains five core modules, namely market intelligence module (M), memory module (Mem), low-level reflection module (L), high-level reflection module (H) and decision-making module (D).

data.value: Five US stocks (AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, TSLA) and ETHUSD. Inputs are daily OHLC and adjusted-close prices, Kline and trading charts, and news from Financial Modeling Prep. Expert guidance comes from Seeking Alpha.
data.quote: We acquired price and news data for all assets from Financial Modeling Prep44 4 FMP API provides data about stock historical price and news, company financial statements, and cryptocurrencies.

window.value: Training period 2022-06-01 to 2023-06-01. Test period 2023-06-01 to 2024-01-01. The full span covers 398 trading days.
window.quote: For dataset split, the data from the latter half of the year is allocated for testing (2023-06-01 \sim 2024-01-01) purposes, while the data from the penultimate year is utilized for training (2022-06-01 \sim 2023-06-01).

models.value: GPT-4 is called via the OpenAI API, with multimodal GPT-4V referenced. No snapshot is given.
models.quote: XML is easy to parse, and extracting fields is simpler, making it an ideal output format for GPT-4.

baselines.value: Twelve baselines: B&H, MACD, KDJ&RSI, ZMR, LGBM, LSTM, Transformer, SAC, PPO, DQN, FinGPT and FinMem.
baselines.quote: We compare and evaluate the trading performance of FinAgent with four widely accepted conventional rule-based trading strategies (B&H, MACD, KDJ&RSI and ZMR) and eight advanced algorithms.

headline_result.value: On TSLA over the test period, FinAgent achieves 92.27% ARR, SR 2.01 and MDD 12.14%, an 84.39% ARR improvement over the best baseline. Average profit improvement is over 36% across 6 datasets.
headline_result.quote: Specifically, a 92.27% return (a 84.39% relative improvement) is achieved on one dataset.

costs.value: The reward function accounts for a commission fee. The fee level is not specified.
costs.quote: The reward function leverages the change of market capitals (earned/lost money) (Liu et al., 2020a) with consideration of commission fee (Sun et al., 2023c; Wang et al., 2021b).

limitations.value: Auxiliary tools are stock-specific, which hurts crypto performance. Results are sensitive to prompt engineering and API randomness, which cannot be controlled. FinAgent accepts slightly higher risk.
limitations.quote: Limitation 3: Result is sensitive to prompt engineering and randomness. In our experiments, we observed a distinct variation in the trading decisions when modifying the decision prompt and executing the agent across different trials.
